finding.claim: The POST /hooks/test route on the `pub` router passes a request-supplied callback URL to axios.post with no validation, so it is an SSRF. The response returns the upstream HTTP status, which lets the caller tell which internal hosts and ports are reachable. A failed connection throws an unhandled error, which is a further oracle. The POST body is fixed to {ping:true}. The route has no auth guard in this file. Whether auth is applied where `pub` is mounted could not be checked, because routes.js is the only file in the directory.

trace.note: `pub` router is created with no auth middleware, unlike `admin`
req.body.callback goes straight into axios.post; axios follows redirects by default
upstream status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist. No private, loopback or link-local blocking, so cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 is reachable. No DNS pinning. No redirect restriction. The `pub` router has no auth middleware here; requireAdmin is applied only to `admin`. The mount point and any app-level auth are not in the repo.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status, with no validation. The `pub` router (routes.js:4) has no auth middleware, since requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` at routes.js:12. The mount point and any app-level auth are not in the repo, so unauthenticated reachability is assumed from the router's name and wiring and is not proven.
